projectSettings.title: Project settings
projectSettings.description: You can change the model, token cap, recon hint, mining hint, verification method and online verification while the audit is running. The audit target, code graph and mining paths can only be changed while the project is paused or completed; the manual-lab note applies only in live-lab mode. Model and phase hints take effect on the next Agent round. When the token cap is reached the project auto-pauses; raise the cap and resume.

projectModel.label: Project model
projectModel.hint: If not set, the global model from Settings is used. Takes effect on the next Agent round (recon / mining / review / verification) after saving.
projectModel.placeholder: Leave blank to use the global model
projectModel.fetchTimeout: Fetching the model list timed out, please try again.

maxToken.label: Max token usage
maxToken.hint: Counts the combined input + output tokens of all this project's Agents. When reached, every phase auto-pauses; raise the cap (or set it to unlimited) in project settings and resume. Blank or 0 means unlimited.
maxToken.invalid: The token cap must be a non-negative integer; 0 means unlimited

advancedOptions.title: Advanced options
advancedOptions.description: Optional. Project model, token cap, recon hint and mining Worker hint do not affect mining paths or the verification method; effective on the next Agent round.
advancedOptions.summary: Project model, token cap, recon hint and mining Worker hint.

attackChain.label: Attack-chain linking
attackChain.hint: After both mining and review finish, tries multi-step chained exploitation of this project's confirmed vulnerabilities to widen the impact. Skipped automatically when fewer than 2 vulnerabilities are confirmed. When a local Docker lab exists, writes a chaining script and dynamically verifies chains that need no user interaction; chains that require interaction (XSS, etc.) skip verification. Off by default.

verifier.label: Verifier (online verification)
verifier.hint: After the Reviewer confirms a front-facing vulnerability, uses FOFA to search for matching internet targets. It first understands the exploit from the report and PoC and runs the original PoC where possible; when no usable HTTP PoC exists it builds a payload from the report rather than skipping; if that fails it adjusts the exploit on the same finding and retries. By default it searches 10 targets per round and stops after 3 successes; otherwise it keeps the successes and searches the next round, up to 5 rounds (50 targets total). Vulnerabilities that would disrupt or tamper with a live service (arbitrary file deletion, DoS, SQL writes, etc.) are only tested after you confirm. Requires a FOFA key in Settings. Off by default.

codeIntel.label: Build call graph
codeIntel.hint: Runs alongside recon. When checked, CodeGraph builds a call graph for src/ so the Worker / Reviewer can look up symbols and calls. The index is written to src/.codegraph/ and rebuilds overwrite the same directory. Failure degrades gracefully and does not block the audit. Off by default to save disk; if enabled mid-run, mining waits for this build to finish. Disabling it deletes this project's index.

off.label: Off
off.hint: The Reviewer does static review only; confirmations use static_only. Default option.

lab.label: Live lab
lab.hint: An isolated-environment round builds a Docker lab (or you provide a manual lab) and reproduces the bug with an HTTP PoC / debug MCP. Evidence level dynamic / mcp.

harness.label: Local verification
harness.hint: No full-project lab. The Reviewer extracts the function, mocks dependencies, and runs a harness in a Docker sandbox. A successful run is recorded as local verification, distinct from a live lab. Falls back to static when Docker is unavailable.

heuristic.label: Heuristic mining
heuristic.hint: After historical-vuln collection finishes, files are weighted and the Worker mines source→sink from high-weight unaudited files. Missing auth, IDOR and business-logic bugs still rely on this path.

lite.label: Lite
lite.hint: Uses only weight-100 files as entry points; lower weights do not block completion. Off by default, which audits every weighted file.

fast.label: Fast scan
fast.hint: After recon, Semgrep matches sinks; a hard code filter then an Agent freezes about 60, and the Fast Worker traces back from each sink. Covers SAST sinks; does not replace heuristic mining.

bypass.label: Historical-vuln bypass
bypass.hint: After historical-vuln collection finishes, each round injects one historical-vuln document and tries to bypass the patch, produce a variant, or confirm an unfixed bug is still exploitable.

unconstrained.label: Unconstrained scan
unconstrained.hint: Starts after historical-vuln collection with a single fixed Worker. Injects only the code map and auth document, dispatching no weighted files. Always uses the bounty gate; the path ends once the Reviewer judges a front-facing bug to have achieved RCE-level impact.

manualLab.label: Manual lab
manualLab.hint: For vulnerability environments that must be set up by hand. Once you fill in the address, credentials and other details, review uses this description first and only falls back to a Docker lab if it is unreachable. You can also add it later in project settings; it takes effect on the next review round.
manualLab.placeholder: e.g. lab at http://127.0.0.1:8080, credentials admin/admin, login at /login. You can also add paths, auth headers, etc.

reconHint.label: Recon hint
reconHint.hint: Optional. Paste text or upload a .txt / .md file as an extra manual hint injected into each recon sub-stage (map/auth, extensions, historical vulns, marking). Do not use it to skip gate tasks; editable while running, effective next round.
reconHint.placeholder: e.g. focus on SSO and admin-panel routes; ignore demo modules; treat the JWT filter as the source of truth for auth.
reconHint.tooLong: Recon hint is too long; max {{max}} characters

workerHint.label: Mining Worker hint
workerHint.hint: Optional. Paste text or upload a .txt / .md file as an extra manual hint injected into every mining round of heuristic, fast scan, historical-vuln bypass and unconstrained scan. Do not use it to shift focus; editable while running, effective next round.
workerHint.placeholder: e.g. focus on admin-panel export and file download; ignore demo accounts; treat the JWT filter as the source of truth for auth.
workerHint.tooLong: Mining hint is too long; max {{max}} characters

hintText.uploadTextFile: Please upload a .txt or .md text file

bounty.label: Bounty mode
bounty.short: Only high-impact bugs exploitable by default
bounty.hint: Records only high-impact classes exploitable by default (RCE, injection, arbitrary file operations, broken access control, stored XSS, 1-click CSRF, source-code hardcoded secrets with server-side impact, etc.). Low-impact items such as CORS, reflected XSS, plain CSRF and missing rate limiting are not recorded; user-changeable passwords in config files and front-end transport-obfuscation AES / publicly shipped keys do not count. Exploitation must hold under the default config or the application's own config options; mark each submission as default or specific config — a risk toggle the vendor already warns about is not "specific config".

full.label: Full mode
full.hint: Beyond high-impact bugs, also records hard-to-exploit items that still demonstrate a real difference (CORS, reflected XSS, missing rate limiting, security headers, plain CSRF, etc.), tagged by the Reviewer as low-impact / hard to exploit.

custom.label: Custom mode
custom.short: Scope decided by a named prompt from Settings
custom.hint: Vulnerability scope is decided entirely by the selected custom prompt (snapshotted into the project), with no bounty-mode hard gate in code. Create a custom audit mode in Settings first.

web.label: Web app
web.hint: Audited as a deployable application: HTTP plus WebSocket / RPC / MQ entry points are treated as sources.

library.label: Library
library.hint: Audited as a component: public APIs / parsers are the caller-controlled entry points. Defaults to local verification with the Verifier off at creation.

mixed.label: Mixed
mixed.hint: Prioritizes the library core; demo/sample/examples are down-weighted. Defaults to local verification with the Verifier off at creation.

exposureModeTooltip.indirectProven:
Indirect consumer: the component has no direct HTTP/RPC entry point, so it cannot be exploited by sending requests to it alone.
Full exploitation depends on an upstream application passing attacker input into the sink (e.g. a SELECT injection point via WallFilter).
The full upstream→component exploit chain has been proven at a real business HTTP/API entry point.
See "### Trigger conditions" in the report for details.
exposureModeTooltip.indirectUnproven:
Indirect consumer: the component has no direct HTTP/RPC entry point, so it cannot be exploited by sending requests to it alone.
Full exploitation depends on an upstream application passing attacker input into the sink (e.g. a SELECT injection point via WallFilter).
The full upstream chain has not been proven at a real business entry point; a harness or unit test calling the component API directly does not count.
Scoring and value tiering already reflect the indirect-consumer constraint (usually lower than a directly remotely exploitable web bug).
See "### Trigger conditions" in the report for details.
exposureModeTooltip.direct: Direct exposure: an attacker can reach the vulnerable sink directly through a user-controlled entry point (HTTP/RPC, etc.), without relying on an upstream application to pass input.

harnessTier.l1: L1: local verification (sink level). A mock harness calls the vulnerable sink function directly to prove the root cause is exploitable — no lab environment needed.
harnessTier.l2: L2: local verification (module level). A mock harness calls module-level functions, covering multiple paths — deeper than L1.
harnessTier.l3: L3: integration verification. Starts the service in a sandbox and runs poc.py to verify the full entry→sink path — equivalent to a live lab test.

fmt.auditModeCustomHint: Vulnerability scope currently follows the project's snapshot of custom mode "{{name}}"; no bounty hard gate. Takes effect on the next round after resuming.

auditModeSelect.addCustomFirst: Add a custom audit mode in Settings first.

bountyScope.title: Bounty mode scope
bountyScope.description: Only records issues that are exploitable by default and cause real impact. Full reference below.
bountyScope.premise: Exploitation must hold under the default config, or by changing only the application's own config options. Mark each submission as default or specific config; a risk toggle the vendor already warns about is not "specific config". Planting files, changing non-application config, or chaining a second independent bug are not allowed. Full mode additionally records items from the "not recorded" list above that still demonstrate a real difference, tagged by the Reviewer as low-impact / hard to exploit.

file_op.note: Read / write / delete / modify / copy / archive traversal, etc.

ssrf_internal.note: Internal network, cloud metadata, or sensitive local ports

stored_xss.note: Must be persisted and execute in another user's browser; do not label reflected XSS as stored

csrf_1click.note: Victim opens a malicious page and immediately triggers RCE or another high-impact action; do not label plain CSRF (profile edits, logout) as 1-click

hardcoded_secret.note: Must be a server-side secret: JWT/HMAC signing, API signing secret, private key, third-party API key, ciphertext inside a protected store/backup, etc.; must enable unauthorized impact

other_impact.note: Must demonstrate code execution, sensitive data disclosure, unauthorized read/write/delete, or arbitrary file operations

ssrf_public.note: Cannot reach internal network / metadata / sensitive local ports

plain_csrf.type: Plain CSRF / just missing a token
plain_csrf.note: Low-impact state changes such as renaming, logout, likes, posts; or requires multiple clicks / confirmation

cors_headers.note: Includes ACAO reflection, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.

open_redirect.note: Unless it can be escalated to auth hijack, token theft, or other real impact

rate_limit.type: Missing rate limit / captcha brute force

weak_random.note: Unless it directly causes an auth bypass

frontend_aes.note: Key is in front-end JS or deliberately shipped publicly; decrypting a field the front end already decrypts / an intercepted login packet is not a CVE

config_default_password.type: Default password in a config file
config_default_password.note: User-changeable passwords or keys in application.yml, .env, compose, docs
